newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says no plan to change A share policy.
newsitem.headline: Manila says no plan to change A share policy.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it had no plan to allow direct foreign ownership of class A shares or to compel companies to merge their A and B shares.
"We at the SEC cannot force companies to declassify their shares, but we welcome the voluntary declassification by some companies," SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay told reporters.
A shares are sold only to Filipino investors, while B shares are open to Filipino and foreign investors. B shares usually trade higher than A shares due to the wider ownership base.
Some companies going public in the past have sold their shares separately to control the level of foreign ownership.

B shares fell earlier on Tuesday as rumours of an imminent policy change swept the market. Hardest hit was Manila Electric Co B, which shed eight pesos to close at 112 as investors sold their holdings in favour of the A shares. First Philippine Holdings Corp B fell 4.50 pesos to 39.

SEC executive director Eugenio Reyes earlier told Reuters the SEC had not issued new rules allowing foreigners to buy A shares. He said foreigners could buy A shares through a trust fund majority-owned by Filipinos.
